rounds.q: Of Americans who drank coffee yesterday, what % had it made at home?
rounds.why: Only 28% had a cup made away from home, so some coffee fans had both.
rounds.src: National Coffee Association, National Coffee Data Trends, Spring 2026 (Jan 2026 survey)
rounds.fun: 82% brewed it at home. Your kitchen is the most popular coffee shop in town!

rounds.q: Of Americans who drank coffee yesterday, what % had some in the evening?
rounds.why: Mornings rule: 86% had coffee first thing in the morning.
rounds.src: National Coffee Association, National Coffee Data Trends, Spring 2026 (Jan 2026 survey)
rounds.fun: Just 11% sip at night. Most of us save the coffee for that first sleepy morning moment!

rounds.q: What % of the world's coffee is grown in Brazil?
rounds.why: Brazil's record crop is 71.9 million of the world's 189.7 million bags, and Vietnam grows about 17%.
rounds.src: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, July 2026 (2026/27 forecast)
rounds.fun: About 38 of every 100 coffee beans start out in Brazil. That's a lot of morning cups!

rounds.q: What % of the tea Americans drink is iced?
rounds.why: The Tea Association says 75 to 80%, so we used the middle. About 86% of US tea is black tea.
rounds.src: Tea Association of the USA, Tea Fact Sheet (iced share undated; black-tea share is 2024 data)
rounds.fun: Most American tea comes with ice cubes. A hot cuppa is the rare treat here!

rounds.q: How many milligrams of caffeine are in an 8-ounce cup of brewed coffee?
rounds.why: A 1-ounce shot of espresso has only about 63 mg, so a plain mug of coffee packs more.
rounds.src: USDA FoodData Central, brewed coffee (40 mg per 100 g, 237 g cup) and espresso (212 mg per 100 g, 29.6 g shot)
rounds.fun: Your plain mug has about 95 mg, beating a 63 mg espresso shot. Sneaky strong!
